vocab.gloss: to think (i.e. to take it to be true that ...) (Usually there is an implication that the notion is mistaken – except when expressing one's own current opinion.)

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ yǐjīng huí jiā le.
example.gloss: I thought you had already gone home.

vocab.gloss: to exceed; to climb over; to surpass

example.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de rén hěn duō.
example.gloss: There are a lot of people in this city.

example.hanzi: 晚上看手機會影響眼睛。
example.pinyin: Wǎnshàng kàn shǒujī huì yǐngxiǎng yǎnjīng.
example.gloss: Looking at your phone at night affects your eyes.

example.hanzi: 我弟弟最喜歡玩這個遊戲。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi zuì xǐhuān wán zhège yóuxì.
example.gloss: My younger brother likes playing this game the most.

vocab.gloss: horse; horse or cavalry piece in Chinese chess; knight in Western chess

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò xiǎng xué qí mǎ.
example.gloss: I want to learn to ride a horse this weekend.

grammar.title: 越來越 + Adjective/Verb (more and more)
grammar.explanation: 越來越 means "more and more". Put it before an adjective or a psychological verb (like 喜歡, 想) to say that the situation keeps changing in that direction. Do not add 很 before the adjective.

examples.gloss: This city is getting bigger and bigger.

examples.hanzi: 我覺得漢語越來越有意思。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde Hànyǔ yuèláiyuè yǒu yìsi.
examples.gloss: I feel Chinese is more and more interesting.
This game is getting harder and harder.

grammar.title: 以為 (mistakenly thought)
grammar.explanation: 以為 introduces something the speaker believed but which turned out not to be true. If you are simply stating a correct opinion, use 覺得 or 想 instead.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù lái le.
Tā yǐwéi zhège chéngshì hěn xiǎo.
examples.gloss: He thought this city was small.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi tā bú huì qí mǎ.
examples.gloss: I thought he couldn't ride a horse.

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.hanzi: 你昨天怎麼沒來?我以為你不想來了。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ zuótiān zěnme méi lái? Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù xiǎng lái le.
dialogue.gloss: Why didn't you come yesterday? I thought you didn't want to come.

dialogue.speaker: 小東
dialogue.hanzi: 對不起,我在家玩遊戲,玩到很晚。
dialogue.pinyin: Duìbùqǐ, wǒ zài jiā wán yóuxì, wán dào hěn wǎn.
dialogue.gloss: Sorry, I was playing games at home, until very late.

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.hanzi: 玩太多遊戲會影響身體,也會影響你的課。
dialogue.pinyin: Wán tài duō yóuxì huì yǐngxiǎng shēntǐ, yě huì yǐngxiǎng nǐ de kè.
dialogue.gloss: Playing too many games affects your health, and your classes too.

dialogue.speaker: 小東
dialogue.hanzi: 我知道。這個城市的人越來越多,週末我想去遠一點的地方走走。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào. Zhège chéngshì de rén yuèláiyuè duō, zhōumò wǒ xiǎng qù yuǎn yìdiǎn de dìfāng zǒuzou.
dialogue.gloss: I know. There are more and more people in this city; on the weekend I want to go somewhere farther away.

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.pinyin: Nà wǒmen qù qí mǎ, hǎo bù hǎo?
dialogue.gloss: Then let's go horse riding, OK?

dialogue.speaker: 小東
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo a! Wǒ yìzhí xiǎng xué qí mǎ.
dialogue.gloss: Sure! I've always wanted to learn to ride a horse.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù lái le.

sentences.gloss: This city is getting bigger and bigger.

sentences.pinyin: Tiānqì huì yǐngxiǎng wǒ de xīnqíng.
Dìdi zài fáng lǐ wán yóuxì.
sentences.gloss: My little brother is playing games in the room.
He is really good at riding horses.

example.hanzi: 這家店的咖啡比較好喝。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de kāfēi bǐjiào hǎo hē.
example.gloss: The coffee at this shop is comparatively better.

example.hanzi: 我最近很忙，都沒去運動。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn hěn máng, dōu méi qù yùndòng.
example.gloss: I've been busy recently and haven't exercised at all.

vocab.gloss: to exchange; to change (clothes etc); to substitute

example.pinyin: Wǒmen huàn yī jiā cāntīng ba.

vocab.gloss: at last; in the end; finally

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngyú mǎi dào piào le!
Nǐ de liǎn zěnme zhème hóng?
example.gloss: Why is your face so red?

vocab.gloss: mouth; classifier for things with mouths (people, domestic animals, cannons, wells etc); classifier for bites or mouthfuls

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ hē le yī kǒu chá.
example.gloss: I only drank one mouthful of tea.

grammar.title: 用「比較」說「比較…一點」
grammar.explanation: 「比較」放在形容詞前面，表示跟別的東西相比時「比較…一點」。在台灣的日常說話裡，常常沒有說出來要比的對象，聽的人自己知道。

examples.hanzi: 捷運比較快，我們搭捷運吧。
examples.pinyin: Jiéyùn bǐjiào kuài, wǒmen dā jiéyùn ba.
examples.gloss: The MRT is faster; let's take the MRT.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de miàn bǐjiào hǎo chī.
examples.gloss: The noodles at this shop taste better.

examples.hanzi: 我最近比較累，想早點睡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn bǐjiào lèi, xiǎng zǎo diǎn shuì.
examples.gloss: I've been rather tired lately; I want to sleep early.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 我最近比較忙，每天都很累。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn bǐjiào máng, měi tiān dōu hěn lèi.
dialogue.gloss: I've been rather busy lately; I'm tired every day.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 你的臉看起來不太好啊。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ de liǎn kàn qǐlái bù tài hǎo a.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 我昨天終於把事情做完了。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān zhōngyú bǎ shìqing zuò wán le.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 那我們換一家店，喝杯茶吧。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà wǒmen huàn yī jiā diàn, hē bēi chá ba.
dialogue.gloss: Then let's switch to another shop and have a cup of tea.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 好啊，我想喝一口溫的茶。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo a, wǒ xiǎng hē yī kǒu wēn de chá.
dialogue.gloss: Sure, I'd like a mouthful of warm tea.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn dōu qí jiǎotàchē shàngbān.
sentences.gloss: Recently I ride a bike to work every day.
Taking the MRT is faster, right?

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù yínháng huàn qián.
sentences.gloss: I'm going to the bank to change money.

sentences.pinyin: Tā xǐ le liǎn jiù qù shàngbān le.
sentences.gloss: He washed his face and then went to work.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ hē le yī kǒu shuǐ.
sentences.gloss: I only drank one mouthful of water.

vocab.gloss: besides; apart from (... also...); in addition to

example.hanzi: 除了牛奶，我還買了兩個蘋果。
example.pinyin: Chúle niúnǎi, wǒ hái mǎi le liǎng ge píngguǒ.
example.gloss: Besides milk, I also bought two apples.

example.hanzi: 他總是騎腳踏車去上班。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì qí jiǎotàchē qù shàngbān.
example.gloss: He always rides a bike to work.

example.hanzi: 她有一雙很漂亮的眼睛。
example.pinyin: Tā yǒu yì shuāng hěn piàoliàng de yǎnjīng.
example.gloss: She has a pair of very pretty eyes.
Yesterday afternoon it suddenly rained heavily.

example.hanzi: 這段路很長，我們慢慢走。
example.pinyin: Zhè duàn lù hěn cháng, wǒmen mànmàn zǒu.
example.gloss: This stretch of road is long; let's walk slowly.

example.hanzi: 醫生說我需要檢查眼睛。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō wǒ xūyào jiǎnchá yǎnjīng.
example.gloss: The doctor said I need to get my eyes examined.

grammar.title: 除了…，還/也… (besides A, also B)
grammar.pattern: 除了 + A（以外），+ 主語 + 還/也 + B
grammar.explanation: 「除了」introduces something that is already true or already included; the second part uses 還 or 也 to add more. In Taiwan you often hear 除了…以外，還… . Keep 除了 at the front of the phrase it marks.

examples.hanzi: 除了中文，他還會說台語。
examples.pinyin: Chúle Zhōngwén, tā hái huì shuō Táiyǔ.
examples.gloss: Besides Chinese, he can also speak Taiwanese.

examples.hanzi: 除了我以外，我們班的人都會游泳。
examples.pinyin: Chúle wǒ yǐwài, wǒmen bān de rén dōu huì yóuyǒng.
examples.gloss: Apart from me, everyone in our class can swim.

examples.hanzi: 我週末除了看書，還常常去運動。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò chúle kàn shū, hái chángcháng qù yùndòng.
examples.gloss: On weekends, besides reading, I also often go exercise.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme le? Kàn qǐlái hěn lèi.
dialogue.gloss: What's wrong? You look really tired.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 我昨天突然頭很痛，今天早上去醫院檢查。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān tūrán tóu hěn tòng, jīntiān zǎoshàng qù yīyuàn jiǎnchá.
dialogue.gloss: Yesterday I suddenly had a bad headache, so this morning I went to the hospital for a check-up.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 他說我這段時間太忙，除了多睡，還要多運動。
dialogue.pinyin: Tā shuō wǒ zhè duàn shíjiān tài máng, chúle duō shuì, hái yào duō yùndòng.
dialogue.gloss: He said I've been too busy lately; besides sleeping more, I also need to exercise more.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 對啊，你總是工作到很晚。
dialogue.pinyin: Duì a, nǐ zǒngshì gōngzuò dào hěn wǎn.
dialogue.gloss: Right, you always work until very late.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 我知道了，這個週末我要去游泳。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào le, zhè ge zhōumò wǒ yào qù yóuyǒng.
dialogue.gloss: I get it — this weekend I'm going swimming.

sentences.gloss: He always goes to bed early.

sentences.pinyin: Tā yǒu yì shuāng dà yǎnjīng.
sentences.gloss: She has a pair of big eyes.

sentences.pinyin: Yīshēng yào jiǎnchá wǒ de shēntǐ.
sentences.gloss: The doctor is going to examine my body.

sentences.pinyin: Chúle niúnǎi wǒ hái yào kāfēi.
sentences.gloss: Besides milk, I also want coffee.
